uncited: It differs from its siblings, [Marching Cubes Surface Normal Estimation](1005-marching-cubes-surface-normal-estimation.md) and [Marching Cubes Surface Area Estimation](1315-marching-cubes-surface-area-estimation.md), by operating on the input scalar field prior to extraction rather than post-processing the resulting mesh geometry.
The input and output arrays share identical dimensions.
The output array `S` uses standard floating-point representation (typically 32-bit or 64-bit float) to store the smoothed scalar field.
This method is specifically chosen to avoid that loss of information.
*   **Time Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
The output array has the same dimensions as the input binary array.
Eliminates jagged artifacts from binary masks.
*   **When to use:** When extracting surfaces from binary segmentation masks (0/1 arrays) and high-quality, smooth geometry is required without losing thin structural details.
*   **When not to use:** When the input is already a continuous signed distance field or scalar volume, or when full control over the smoothing kernel parameters is required.
It was introduced to address the common issue where segmentation methods produce binary masks that result in poor-quality meshes when extracted directly.
